simple.meaning: לַחַשׁ (lachash) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, a whisper , i.e. by implication, (in a good sense) a private prayer , (in a bad one) an incantation ; concretely, an amulet.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: לַחַשׁ (H3908) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ecclesiastes 10:11, with occurrences in Ecclesiastes, Isaiah, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to לַחַשׁ (H3908) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in לַחַשׁ (H3908) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: לַחַשׁ (lachash) / H3908 is traced through Ecclesiastes 10:11, Isaiah 3:3, Isaiah 3:20, Isaiah 26:16 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H3908. lachash לַ֫חַשׁ noun [masculine] a whispering, charming ; — ׳ל Isa 26:16 ; לָ֑חַשׁ Eccl 10:11 ; Isa 3:3 ; Jer 8:17 ; plural לְחָשִׁים Isa 3:20 . — 1 serpent-charming Eccl 10:11 ; לָ֑חַשׁ נְבוֺן Isa 3:3 (probably more General). 2 charms, amulets , worn by women, Isa 3:20 . 3 whisper of prayer , לַחַשׁ צָקוּן Isa 26:16 they pour forth a whisper of prayer (but Koppe Bö Gr Di Du read לַחַשׁ צְקוֺן 'Zauberzwang,' compulsion of (by) magic ).
